content.en: Researchers are using algorithms to improve the accuracy of estimating wear on wheel-rail contact in railway systems. They are also developing and validating wear models for predicting wheel and rail profile evolution, as well as evaluating the impact of wheel-rail contact and dynamic forces. Algorithms implemented in MATLAB and SIMPACK are being used to simulate and predict wear and damage in railway vehicles and tracks. These advancements aim to enhance the safety and efficiency of railway systems.
content.da: Forskere bruger algoritmer til at forbedre nøjagtigheden af estimater for slid på kontaktpunkterne mellem hjul og skinner i jernbanesystemer. De udvikler og validerer også slidmodeller til at forudsige udviklingen af hjul- og skinneprofiler, samt vurderer påvirkningen af hjul-skinne-kontakt og dynamiske kræfter. Algoritmer implementeret i MATLAB og SIMPACK bruges til at simulere og forudsige slid og skader i jernbanevogne og spor. Disse fremskridt har til formål at forbedre sikkerheden og effektiviteten i jernbanesystemer.

critic.en: Are you telling me that the future of railways is now in the hands of algorithms? So, we're just gonna sit back and let machines decide how much our trains should wear out and when they should be repaired?
critic.da: Er algoritmer virkelig den hellige gral? Hvad sker der med de mennesker, der hidtil har bygget deres liv og arbejdsliv omkring denne ekspertise?

potential.en: That's fantastic! Predictive maintenance can help prevent accidents and reduce operational costs in railway systems. I'm curious, have you had the chance to see how these algorithms in MATLAB and SIMPACK are applied in a real-world railway maintenance setting?
potential.da: Hvorfor er du så begejstret for denne forskningsindsats? Er det sikkerheden, effektiviteten, eller måske noget helt andet, der driver din interesse?
